summary: Eleven labels print chlorophyllin at 100 or 132 mg and one prints chlorophyll at 50 mg; printed purposes are skin, digestive and metabolic, or none. The stored paper (7350215) is an uncontrolled 1980 report of 62 nursing home patients. 11724948 is a real RCT of 100 mg chlorophyllin three times a day in 180 adults, with a named primary endpoint, positive on a urinary aflatoxin biomarker; it doesn't test a purpose these labels print. 16417778 reports leukopenia response with no named primary outcome. No plain chlorophyll efficacy trial was found in the two searches; 19952359 is a three-volunteer unblinded pharmacokinetic study. Topical trials are not used.

population.description: 180 healthy adults from Qidong, China, at high risk from dietary aflatoxin.

outcomes.name: Urinary aflatoxin-N7-guanine at 3 months: 55% lower median than placebo (P = 0.036)

limitations: A biomarker of exposure; no clinical outcome. Population has unavoidable dietary aflatoxin exposure.
